title: Tanzanian Cassava Chips
community: Coastal Tanzania and Zanzibar — the cassava chip tradition
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Muhogo Chips — cassava cut into thick chips and deep-fried until golden and crispy, served with pili pili and lime. The coastal alternative to potato chips — denser, chewier, and with a more complex starchy flavour. Found at every beach and street market on the Tanzanian coast.
longDesc: Muhogo chips are the coastal Tanzanian alternative to potato chips — thick-cut cassava pieces deep-fried until the outside is crispy and golden and the inside is dense, starchy, and slightly chewy. They are served at every coastal food stall and are the default snack of the Tanzanian coast.
ingredients: 600g cassava — peeled and cut into thick rectangular chips
Pili Pili (TZA117) and lime wedges to serve
steps: Peel cassava. Cut into 8—10cm rectangular chips.
Boil cassava chips in salted water for 12—15 minutes until just tender but not falling apart. Drain.
Fry in batches for 6—8 minutes until golden and crispy on the outside.
Serve with pili pili and lime.
chefTips: Pre-boiling is essential — raw cassava fries poorly and unevenly.
Pat completely dry after boiling — moisture causes dangerous oil splatter.
They need longer in the oil than potato chips — cassava is denser.
commonMistakes: Skipping the boil — raw cassava fries unevenly.
cookingScience: Unlike potatoes, cassava contains very little pectin — its cell walls are held together primarily by starch. Pre-boiling gelatinises this starch, creating a stable interior structure. Without pre-boiling, the raw starch produces a dense, gummy interior even after extended frying.
sustainabilityTips: Cassava is Tanzania's most climate-resilient crop — drought-tolerant and widely grown.
healthBenefits: Lower glycaemic index than potato chips.
culturalNote: Muhogo chips are the coast's answer to every chip craving — denser, more substantial, and with the particular starchy satisfaction that only cassava provides. On the coast, they are as fundamental as potato chips elsewhere.
